title: The bro-harness/daemon boundary: standalone process contract
content: The shared contract bottom keeps cross-boundary types pure: `bro-core` owns ids/refs/errors and `bro-protocol` owns session control plus status/view DTOs. `bro-harness` remains an independently buildable library+binary but `blackbox` MUST NOT depend on or link `bro-harness`, `bro-code-mode`, V8, or `bro-capabilities`; Cargo enforces the process boundary. Every harness-backed provider dispatch runs in one standalone `bro-harness` child. stdin NDJSON carries user turns and controls, stdout NDJSON carries the Claude-compatible event envelope, and the child writes its durable event log under the explicitly passed `BRO_HOME`. Daemon capabilities cross only through the complete server-filtered MCP catalog. The compatibility flat names `corpus_search` and `atom_invoke` alias `bbox_corpus_search` and `atom_invoke` from that catalog without hiding qualified MCP tools, and fail closed when the source server/tool is unavailable. Provider credentials stay in the harness child and are scrubbed from shell grandchildren; project build env travels separately through `shell_env`. V8/code-mode lives inside the harness child, while the `isolate` binary remains independently executable. The thin fleet client (`bro-cli` via `bro-fleet-client`) depends only on `bro-protocol` + `bro-core`, never either runtime implementer. See `design/bro-harness/harness-process-boundary.md`.
